news.body:

news.body:
株式会社SNK宣布，好评发售中的对战格斗游戏《饿狼传说：群狼之城》第3季第6位DLC角色，“拉奥·高迪亚姆斯”（以下简称拉奥）今日上线。
为庆祝拉奥参战，世界知名动画师大张正己特别制作了一支描绘拉奥全新战斗的动画宣传片。敬请欣赏由大张正己以其标志性的动感影像风格呈现的拉奥故事。
出生于日本广岛县。G-1NEO工作室代表取缔役CEO。身为动画创作人、机甲设计师、导演，参与过许多人气动画作品的制作。他以极具动感的绘画和独特的变形方式建立了自己的演绎风格。 这种演绎风格得到了全世界动画迷的支持，并对许多动画创作人产生了重大影响。在电视动画片《Battle Fighters 饿狼传说》系列中担任角色设计和美术总监，在剧场版《饿狼传说 THE MOTION PICTURE》中担任导演。此外，他还制作了《THE KING OF FIGHTERS XV》的特别影片，以及《饿狼传说：群狼之城》的特别音乐视频。
追寻“玛尔斯斗衣”的强敌——“拉奥”究竟是何方神圣？
拉奥・高迪亚姆斯 | LAOCORN GAUDEAMUS
声优 ［日语］三木真一郎 ［英语］Branden Loera
“拉奥”登场于1994年上映的剧场版动画《饿狼传说 -THE MOTION PICTURE-》，是阻挡在特瑞等人面前的强敌之一。他是高迪亚姆斯一族的后裔，也是“苏莉亚·高迪亚姆斯”的双胞胎哥哥，率领忠诚的黑暗三结众，一直在收集据说寄宿着斗神之力的“玛尔斯斗衣”。他的目的只有一个：超越人类的领域，成为“神”。
这一次，得知最后一件斗衣留在南镇，而且将被带给“拳皇”的优胜者后，拉奥亲自降临了战斗的舞台。在获得最后一件斗衣之后，等待着他的命运究竟是……。
敬请欣赏全新登场的劲敌“拉奥”强大而华丽的身姿，以及其战斗风格吧。

《饿狼传说 -THE MOTION PICTURE-》简介
1994年7月16日上映的剧场版动画作品，改编自SNK的对战格斗游戏《饿狼传说》系列。影片由松竹负责发行，松竹、富士电视台、SNK和旭通国际共同制作。导演由曾担任电视特别节目《格斗战士 饿狼传说》系列角色设计及总作画监督的大张正己先生担任。
剧情围绕蕴含重大神力的“玛尔斯斗衣”，描绘了特瑞·博加德等人与高迪亚姆斯一族后裔拉奥·高迪亚姆斯之间的激烈战斗。以拉奥和他的双胞胎妹妹苏莉亚为首的电影原创角色登场，展开了与游戏不同的全原创剧情。
在《饿狼传说：群狼之城》中，代表本作的原创角色拉奥作为可游玩角色参战。他追寻着“玛尔斯斗衣”，时隔约30年登上《饿狼传说》系列的游戏正篇，展开全新的战斗。
《饿狼传说：群狼之城》是一款最新的格斗游戏，兼具了任何人都能享受的爽快操作性和随着游戏深入而扩展的策略深度。它继承了系列特有的魅力，同时还搭载了独特的艺术风格、新的战斗系统“REV”、单人RPG模式“EOST”等众多易于上手的元素，适合初次接触的玩家。
此外，官方彻底追求适合初学者的操作风格，以及通过跨平台联机/回滚方式带来的舒适在线对战。
第3季中，除了新角色外，还计划每月持续发布新的关卡和各种游戏内内容。发售后也将通过定期的内容更新，促进玩家社区的活跃和提升游戏品牌的长期价值。
在第3季中，以“背负复仇命运者”为概念，瑞克·斯托德、达克·金、金家藩等往年人气角色参战。此外，在10月的DLC角色第4弹中，同时上线佐野万次郎（Mikey）和龙宫寺坚（Draken）两名角色，11月上线拉奥，作为第三季的收官，来自《铁拳》的丽奈将于12月加入战斗。第3季共追加7名DLC角色。

news.title: Report: GTA 6 Generated Nearly $2B in Sales by Launch Day
news.summary_raw: GTA 6 reportedly generated $1.84 billion from approximately 19 million copies sold by launch day. This will likely be one of the biggest entertainment experience launches of all time in any industry.

members.title: Report: GTA 6 Generated Nearly $2B in Sales by Launch Day
18 unsolicited third-party statistics about GTA 6

news.body:
Report: GTA 6 Generated Nearly $2B in Sales by Launch Day
GTA 6 reportedly generated $1.84 billion from approximately 19 million copies sold by launch day. This will likely be one of the biggest entertainment experience launches of all time in any industry.
In case you missed it
GTA Tech
Rockstar Games
Grand Theft Auto VI has reportedly generated approximately $1.84 billion in sales revenue by its release day, potentially making Rockstar Games’ blockbuster the largest video game launch in history. Not bad.
The figure comes from analytics company Sensor Tower, which estimates that GTA 6 had sold approximately 19.05 million copies as of the morning of the game's launch. Roughly 75% of those sales reportedly came from PlayStation, with Xbox accounting for the remaining quarter.
These are not official sales figures from Rockstar Games or parent company Take-Two Interactive. Take-Two has remained deliberately cautious about announcing numbers, only confirming in its latest financial report that pre-orders were “tracking far above our initial expectations.”
Rockstar Games
Sensor Tower estimates that more than $1.5 billion of the current total came from pre-orders. That would considerably exceed the already historic projections circulating earlier this year. Analysts already speculated that GTA 6 could make at least $1 billion in pre-launch sales.
Demand reportedly accelerated after Rockstar premiered its extended GTA 6 gameplay presentation through Netflix in August. Sensor Tower estimates that the showcase produced a sixfold increase in pre-orders, demonstrating how effectively Rockstar converted years of anticipation into sales without relying on a conventional marketing rollout.
The estimated $1.84 billion total is more than twice the approximately $800 million GTA 5 generated during its first day in 2013. GTA 5 needed three days to cross $1 billion, at the time becoming the fastest entertainment release to reach that milestone.
GTA 6 may have passed that benchmark before its first complete day on sale. Sensor Tower’s estimate also places its launch revenue above the entire $1.805 billion global theatrical run attributed to Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, although comparing game sales with theatrical box-office revenue is not entirely like-for-like.
The commercial response follows similarly extraordinary critical reception. GTA 6 currently holds a 99 Metascore, making it the highest-rated game in Metacritic history while matching the average held by the original version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time across a substantially larger number of published reviews.
Reviewers have particularly praised the density and reactivity of Leonida. Rockstar developed new or substantially redesigned technology for animation retargeting, localized weather, ray-traced lighting, audio propagation, NPC behavior, police identification, character appearance, and numerous smaller physical interactions. We recently examined those systems in our technical breakdown of GTA 6.
The launch has been large enough to place pressure on the surrounding infrastructure as well. PlayStation Network experienced a confirmed service disruption only hours before release, with thousands of users reporting problems accessing games and online features. Services were subsequently restored, although the timing reinforced expectations that GTA 6 would place unprecedented demand on console networks.
Analysts now expect GTA 6 to surpass $3 billion in revenue and 30 million copies by the end of 2026. Whether those projections prove accurate will not be clear until Take-Two publishes official figures, but the available estimates suggest Rockstar has already delivered the largest entertainment launch of the year, and possibly the largest video game release ever.

news.title: Ubisoft lays off 166 in Canada across Montréal and Quebec City
news.summary_raw: The cuts come from the Montréal and Quebec City offices, two studios that have historically benefited from sizable subsidies offered by the Canadian government to bolster the country's game development industry.

members.title: Ubisoft lays off 166 in Canada across Montréal and Quebec City
Ubisoft lays off 166 staff in Montreal and Quebec studios

news.body:
Ubisoft has confirmed that the company has cut 166 jobs in Montréal and Quebec City today, attributing the layoffs to ever-changing production needs.
The 166 positions come mostly from production and support roles, according to GamesIndustry.biz. Some proportion of that number is made up of employees from Vantage Studio, Ubisoft's joint-venture with Tencent that oversees Assassin's Creed, Far Cry, and Rainbow Six—the company's biggest moneymaking franchises. The collaborative division was founded in 2025, uniting studios from Montréal, Quebec, Sherbrooke, Saguenay, Barcelona, and Sofia to focus on a few properties.
Gamesindustry.biz reports that the layoffs were due to cancelled projects or ones that had been significantly rescoped, but there is no word from Ubisoft of what those projects might be.
"We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognize the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources," Ubisoft said in a statement.
These layoffs come months after Ubisoft shuttered its Halifax studio which also, like today's studios, saw massive tax breaks and subsidies through local employment-boosting programs in Canada. Today's layoffs are a hard hit to studios that make up a foundational part of the region's game development scene.

复刻实体卡牌魅力，打造多元集卡新体验
传统卡牌游戏大多以对战为核心，IP角色被套进成熟的战斗模板，服务于数值养成。而《群星漫卡》跳出了传统卡牌手游、常规IP改编产品的固有框架，其核心体验的起点十分新颖——在手机上还原实体卡牌最有魅力的拆卡瞬间。本次首曝宣传PV开篇，几大人气国漫IP化作卡包，随着卡包的撕开，内藏的卡牌依次释出，直观展示不同国漫角色、不同稀有等级卡牌的卡面美术与工艺质感，将线下拆卡包的仪式感与爽快感原汁原味还原，让玩家随时随地享受拆卡的乐趣。
依托姚记集团在卡牌制作领域多年沉淀的工艺积累，游戏在数字卡牌视觉上进行了深度打磨，PV依次展示了《斗罗大陆》《狐妖小红娘》《吞噬星空》三大首发IP卡牌效果，不同稀有度卡牌拥有差异化卡面与特殊边框，镭射、光栅、流麻等热门实体工艺在数字端动态呈现，借电子卡牌的独特工艺优势，为国漫人气角色赋予更出众的视觉表现，让每张卡牌都具备独立的观赏收藏价值，而非单纯的战力工具。
收藏与情怀是集换卡牌的灵魂，《群星漫卡》深度挖掘国漫IP内容，设计了丰富的电子主题收藏册。玩家可以收集SSR唐三、SSR昊天锤等卡牌解锁特殊搭配，集齐涂山红红、东方月初经典CP名场面，将原著中的经典角色组合、剧情高光时刻定格在卡册，随时翻看品味，让卡牌承载IP情怀，满足每名“收藏家”的收藏乐趣。
除收藏玩法外，游戏也提供轻度策略对战。玩家在《群星漫卡》中可以随心构筑属于自己的IP卡组，实现斗罗、狐妖跨IP碰撞。轻度对战是IP互动的拓展，进一步丰富受众体验，让收藏到的卡牌拥有实实在在的使用场景。同时，跨IP卡组对战天然充满想象空间，有望激发各式UGC内容与玩家讨论话题，助力社区生态快速成长。
多IP集结长线布局，让每一个国漫IP持续焕发新生
不同于市面上大多以单一IP为核心的IP衍生产品，多IP并行的长线运营思路，正是《群星漫卡》最核心的差异化优势。游戏首曝即官宣集结《斗罗大陆》《狐妖小红娘》《吞噬星空》三大国民级国漫IP，把分属不同世界观、拥有各自独立粉丝圈层的人气角色与故事内容汇聚在同一个卡牌世界。与此同时，阅文集团CEO侯晓楠也曾明确表示，多部国漫IP在同步筹备接入《群星漫卡》中，让IP池具备充足的拓展空间。这样大规模、跨作品的IP集结，在当前国内游戏产品中实属罕见。阅文集团对IP的投入力度，也侧面说明了他们对这款游戏的信心和决心。
《群星漫卡》打造的多IP生态，将实现不同圈层粉丝的互通流动，打破单一IP自带的用户天花板，让喜爱不同国漫的玩家能够在同一个平台相遇、交流。更重要的是，游戏内卡牌收集、交换、对战的独特玩法，为IP开辟了一条全新的长线生命力通道。以往IP内容大多依托动画、小说的更新节奏，热度容易随剧情周期起伏，而在《群星漫卡》里，角色、名场面被转化为可收集、可品鉴、可组卡对战的电子卡牌，IP内容可以持续拆分、包装、上新，即便原作剧情告一段落，粉丝也能通过抽卡、收藏、构筑卡组的方式持续和喜爱的角色、故事产生互动，让IP热度得以长效延续。
海量国漫IP的集结，同样承载着传播国漫文化的价值。借助电子卡牌这种受众接受度高、流通性强的新载体，《群星漫卡》让国漫IP不再局限于原有的内容，从而将风格各异的国产故事、经典角色高光时刻带给更多玩家，持续传递国产原创故事魅力，助力国漫文化出圈。游戏在首曝日即打出“国漫IP大集结”的目标，在阅文海量IP储备与姚记成熟卡牌产业能力的相互赋能下，这一极具探索性的目标，已经在向实现的方向不断稳步地前进。

members.title: Adjust 发布《2026 年移动应用趋势区域聚焦：土耳其》报告

news.body:
—— 洞察游戏、电商与金融市场新趋势，助力中国企业把握土耳其出海机遇
中国北京，2026年11月19 日讯——全球领先的监测与分析公司 Adjust 今日发布《2026 年移动应用趋势区域聚焦：土耳其》报告。报告深入剖析了土耳其移动应用市场的最新格局，指出该国在游戏、电商、金融等核心领域展现出差异化且强劲的增长特征。对于致力于拓展海外市场的中国出海企业而言，精准把握这些细分差异将是制定本地化产品与营销策略、抢占市场先机的关键一步。
土耳其：从应用消费市场走向全球数字产业舞台
土耳其拥有 8,770 万人口，移动连接渗透率达到 93.3%，互联网用户更是高达 7,750 万，人口年龄中位数仅为 33.5 岁。在数字消费市场持续扩大的同时，本土数字产业也在加速发展：2025 年土耳其电商交易额达到 1,154.3 亿美元，同比增长 52.2%；本土游戏开发商全球收入达到 27.6 亿美元，较 2020 年增长 450%。值得关注的是，土耳其游戏开发商的全球收入远高于本土玩家的游戏支出，反映出当地数字产业已具备面向全球市场发展的能力。
游戏：从安装规模转向用户参与质量
2026 年上半年，土耳其游戏应用会话量同比增长 6%，平均会话时长达到 33.69 分钟，较两年前增长 8%。其中，中度游戏仅占安装量的 12%，却贡献了 51% 的会话量，显示不同游戏类型的用户参与程度存在明显差异。
电商：增长机会在于把新用户转化为长期客户
2026 年上半年，土耳其电商应用会话量同比增长 4%，高于全球 0.3% 的增幅。尽管 D1 表现亮眼，但在 D7 留存率上，土耳其与 MENAT 地区及全球基准趋同，均为 6%，这意味着长效留存的挑战依然存在。
金融：细分赛道增长与用户信任同样重要
土耳其金融应用的 D30 留存率达到 4%，是全球平均水平的两倍，表现出较强的用户持续使用能力。其中，股票交易应用安装量和会话量分别同比增长 41% 和 43%，成为值得关注的细分领域。
对于计划拓展当地金融科技市场的企业而言，这意味着不能只关注用户获取，还需要围绕安全性、服务透明度和用户体验建立信任，推动用户关系长期发展。
以数据驱动增长，把握市场机会
面对不同应用品类的增长差异，企业需要的不只是市场规模数据，更需要持续了解用户获取、参与和留存表现，以便及时优化营销策略。
Adjust META 区域销售总监 Başak Zerman 表示：“土耳其科技行业不仅在全球舞台上证明了自身价值，也持续吸引着全球巨额投资。要想在 2026 年抢占风口，我们的举措就必须精准。将预测性 AI 数据分析与隐私优先型监测相结合，营销人员就能将高价值的资本转化为长效 ROI。”
土耳其市场的增长潜力值得关注，但不同品类的用户行为和增长逻辑并不相同。中国企业出海需要基于当地数据，判断市场机会、优化获客策略，并持续提升用户留存与变现效率。Adjust《2026 年移动应用趋势区域聚焦：土耳其》通过对游戏、金融、购物和电商应用安装量、会话量、会话时长及用户留存表现的分析，为企业了解当地市场和制定移动增长策略提供参考。
获取完整版报告，欢迎点击此处或发送邮件至 china-marketing@adjust.com 。

Adjust 是 AppLovin (纳斯达克代码：APP) 旗下公司，旨在帮助海量应用实现从移动端到CTV等多平台的监测和增长，深受全球营销者的信赖。无论是快速增长的数字品牌，还是试水应用领域的实体公司，Adjust 都能为其应用营销旅程保驾护航。Adjust 强大的监测与分析套件能够为营销人员提供营销必备工具，助力其业务增长。

news.title: This Spider-Man Simulation Brings Back Memories Of Sticky Wall-Crawler Toys
news.summary_raw: We also got a peek into Duncan Tune's workflow.

members.title: This Spider-Man Simulation Brings Back Memories Of Sticky Wall-Crawler Toys

news.body:
This Spider-Man Simulation Brings Back Memories Of Sticky Wall-Crawler Toys
We also got a peek into Duncan Tune's workflow.
Duncan Tune has clearly struck a nostalgic chord with this project, reminding people of those sticky toys. And, of course, everyone loves Spider-Man. As he explained, he's always looking for inspiration to experiment with Vellum dynamics in Houdini: it's a fun set of tools for creating quick simulations with impressive detail. He initially started with a gecko model, inspired by the toys he actually played with as a kid, but wanted to take the idea in a more unexpected direction. He then tested the idea with Star Wars stormtroopers before settling on Spider-Man.
"The first thing is to prep the model for simulation. I found the model on Sketchfab and just took a single frame of the crawl animation that came with it – you always want regular-sized triangulation across the whole model for Vellum simulation. Ideally, you want the mesh used in the simulation to be a proxy for the original model; therefore, you can make it as low-poly as possible and can use a VDB to combine all the geo into a single mesh. Because of the fingers, I couldn't go super low-poly, but I pushed it as far as I dared.
Next was to find the right constraints for getting that stretchy feel – I tried cloth with struts or pressure, but they always feel like a deflated football. I then tried tetrahedral stretch after seeing a brilliant tutorial by Ghost3Dee for a crawling creature which, after a lot of tweaking, gave me exactly the sort of jell-o wobble and volume-preserving stretch I was looking for."
"For the simulation, the wall is made into a pinned, unmoving cloth surface so that glue constraints can be created between it and the Spider-Men. The glue constraints have a breaking threshold, so they slowly break as gravity pulls on the mesh
The Spider-Men are emitted every few frames from one moving and rotating mesh, giving variation to each instance. The geo is also given IDs and a class attribute based on the frame it's emitted, which is used later for swapping in the original model. An initial point velocity is also added to give the Spider-Men the speed to fly at the wall.
Whilst this broadly worked, I was finding that the breaking threshold was difficult to get right. Too high and the Spider-Man would stay put, too low and the model would slide down the wall without tumbling. So, to vary this attribute, I used a noise that slid downwards and remapped the breaking threshold with this noise. It meant that localized thresholds would rise and fall over time, parts of the body would break free from the wall, and gravity would pull the mesh in interesting directions, depending on where it was still glued.
Because the constraints are quite weak – the mesh doesn't need to be very stiff – you don't need many substeps for the simulation, but even so, the 8 seconds of simulation took 12 hours to cache.
Then comes, for me, the magic part. I use point deform on almost every project, but it still amazes me with how well it works. For this project, I used it to replace the proxy mesh with the original one using a "for each loop" and the class and ID attributes I created earlier. In the "for each loop", you can transfer any other attributes too (such as color variations) and smooth out the distorted mesh, if required.
The shading and lighting were very simple, really. It used subsurface scattering to give you that tangible rubber feel, with light passing through the thinnest parts of the mesh, something which is emphasized by the extreme stretching and thinning of the fingers, arms, and legs. I used warm and cool lights to give it a dusk/dawn feel, a favored time of day in the Spider-Man films!"
Duncan Tune
Duncan Tune

members.title: Clever Weight-Painting Tool For Better Character Deformations

news.body:
Clever Weight-Painting Tool For Better Character Deformations
Black magic.
3D Artist known as Flat has been sharing their progress on a cyborg ninja lady that looks somewhat like Gray Fox from Metal Gear Solid. They've shown different stages of the process, from modeling her complex, layered armor to rigging the character.
Getting the shoulders and armpits right is notoriously tricky, often resulting in harsh weight transitions that cause mesh deformation. In their latest demo, the artist showed how the Volume Smoothing mode in the Smooth Weights add-on can smooth weights across meshes that aren't physically connected. It really looks like magic and seems like a tool many Blender rigging artists could use. However, not everyone liked the character's new flesh-like design, some felt the original version was more interesting.
Volume Smoothing blends weights based on proximity rather than topology, letting it smooth across gaps and overlapping geometry. Smooth Weights was developed by Brave Rabbit, who also created a tool that brings RBF to Blender through a node-based solver.
For weight painting, Flat uses cvELD Edit Paint, which allows for painting and fine-tuning weights for multiple bones without leaving Edit Mode. cvELD also has a handy tool for helping fix clipping and gaps between the body and clothing.

You might also want to check out Fuyumidori's chest anatomy showcase and Igor Silva's RBF muscle setup.

news.title: Why greenlighting Dressmaker wasn't an easy decision to make
news.summary_raw: Pre-production data said Dressmaker might not find an audience. Free Lives pushed past those numbers to make a bona fide hit.

members.title: Why greenlighting Dressmaker wasn't an easy decision to make

news.body:
Why greenlighting Dressmaker wasn't an easy decision to make
Pre-production data said Dressmaker might not find an audience. Free Lives pushed past those numbers to make a bona fide hit.
Cozy Lives and Free Lives' Dressmaker is the surprise sleeper indie hit of 2026. It's racked up thousands of 'overwhelmingly positive' reviews on Steam and driven conversation among developers about how the industry may be missing out on certain audiences by ignoring different types of gameplay. But while it's got tongues wagging now, there was a moment in pre-production where its makers weren't sure the game would actually find its audience.
That's according to Dressmaker programmer and designer Ruan Rothman, who explained to GameDeveloper.com that Free Lives has spent years building a process to identify game ideas that are creatively interesting and have commercial viability. Answering the question of "what game to make" may seem obvious, but it can be a daunting task for game developers. Just because you're excited about a game, does it mean that there's an audience who will share your passion?
And even if there's an audience, can you make the game in a way that fits an appropriate scope and budget? Savvy developers everywhere have long sought ways to mitigate the risks that come with the hit-driven nature of video game development—and Free Lives' process begins with releasing prototypes on Itch.io.
Free Lives uses game jams and itch prototypes to blend passion and commercial potential
Free Lives built its process based on a concept almost everyone in the game industry can relate to: nobody can "reliably intuitively tell" whether a game can be creatively and commercially viable. So in the last few years, the studio adopted "a set of heuristics" to help judge which games were worth pursuing.
"We try to be as empirical as possible in our approach," Rothman explained in a conversation that came after we spoke with him and artist Sara Laubscher on the GameDeveloper.com podcast. "Every pitch needs a playable prototype, usually hosted on itch.io. The first test is whether the prototype gains traction on that platform, specifically regarding engagement and downloads."
"The second [test] is whether the game gets a response on social media, so we might create a mini-trailer or post gameplay clips online to gauge the response. Finally, if content creators spontaneously create videos of the game (usually YouTube), that's another great signal. Even more compelling, is when the videos of your game/prototype are overperforming on those channels relative to the average views the content creator gets." He noted that the team is aware this process risks burning through a game's marketing momentum. If an influencer plays the early prototype two years before the game comes out, interest in the game can be hard to maintain or "regenerate."
Image via Cozy Lives/Free Lives
These aren't "hard and fast rules," he said, so subjective judgment remains "inevitable" in the process. But the stakes are high. "The worst possible outcome in game development is spending years on a game that nobody wants," Rothman said. "Besides the obvious financial implications, even if your studios survives, it's devastating for morale."
With so much adoration that's greeted Dressmaker since it made its public debut, you'd think there was existing interest built on that process. According to Rothman, that wasn't the case, and the question of whether or not to proceed with development required discussion and debate. The first Dressmaker prototype that emerged from Free Lives' internal game jam "wasn't quite playable," but was sufficient to make test posts on Instagram. The reaction justified the decision to then greenlight a free itch.io-ready prototype, eventually scoring 10,000 downloads in its first month on the platform.
Unfortunately that's a relatively low number for Free Lives' prototypes. Another of its games, Stick it to the Stickman racked up over 100,000 downloads. There wasn't any organic content creator uptake, and no publishers reached out to discuss signing the title. This all made the "signal" of Dressmaker difficult to understand, especially since the Free Lives team had never made a "cozy game" before.
Despite the low numbers, there was reason to keep testing. Because even though Stick it to the Stickman was downloaded more often, it wound up "underperforming" after being released on Steam. Ruan said it made the Free Lives team wonder if itch.io was still a "reliable predictor" for Steam success.
So the team initiated another marketing push on social media and reached out for a few influencers. Again, the response on Instagram and TikTok seemed to show there was an audience out there excited about a dressmaking game, so they decided to proceed cautiously ahead under a "limited" scope. Luckily, it paid off in spades.
What's the lesson from a surprise hit?
By now you've probably heard over and over again how "data-driven approaches" are essential to succeed in the modern game industry. Except in the case of Dressmaker, the data was telling a story that could have gone one way or another. So it's worth asking—does Rothman think the Free Lives team learned anything from this experience?
"I don't think we've figured that out just yet!" he admitted. "We now know that you need multiple corroborating signals in order to trust that a project has appeal, and that any one single metric can be quite unreliable. We've had some prototypes get great traction on social media, but then fail to convert to prototype downloads or success on Steam."
Keep in mind that Free Lives isn't some big publisher looking to turn game development into a factory line process with perfectly-predicted marketing. Rothman said the studio is filled with people who want to make "culturally relevant, standout hit games." "We don't want to simply tread water by breaking even on a project to project basis," he said.
Ironically, that means the search for stability—even when backed by a data-driven approach—means planning to take risks. Rothmann said Free Lives' next games are "likely to again, be so completely different than anything else we've done."
"And the development scene is changing faster than ever before," he added. "So who knows?"

news.title: US Senate hearing examines child safety on Roblox, considers bipartisan bill to bypass forced arbitration
news.summary_raw: The US Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism held a hearing this week to examine child safety on Roblox and consider a bipartisan bill that would allow families and victims to bypass forced arbitration.

members.title: US Senate hearing examines child safety on Roblox, considers bipartisan bill to bypass forced arbitration

news.body:
US Senate hearing examines child safety on Roblox, considers bipartisan bill to bypass forced arbitration
Roblox argues "a legal position about arbitration is not a measure of a company's safety record, and a hearing built around it fails to advance safety"
The US Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism held a hearing this week to examine child safety on Roblox and consider a bipartisan bill that would allow families and victims to bypass forced arbitration.
As Bloomberg reports, the No Forced Arbitration for Child Sexual Exploitation and Cyber Injuries Act, introduced by Senators Josh Hawley and Dick Durbin, would allow those affected to pursue legal action in public court, even if they previously agreed to private arbitration in a company's terms of use.
In response, Roblox global head of public policy Nicky Jackson Colaço told Wired: "Safety has been central to Roblox since we launched. We require age checks for chat, place users under 16 in age-based accounts with protective defaults, and block images and video in chat."
"A legal position about arbitration is not a measure of a company's safety record, and a hearing built around it fails to advance safety. Protecting children online takes stronger protections, better tools, and consistent standards that apply everywhere kids spend time online."
During the hearing, Senator Hawley criticised Roblox's child safety record, stating it failed to address issues because doing so would "threaten their user count, and therefore their revenues."
"If your children are on Roblox, they are being exposed in all likelihood to sexual predators," he added.
Roblox CEO David Baszucki declined to testify in court. In a letter obtained by Bloomberg, he stated that "Roblox continues to welcome the discussion of how online platforms protect young people online."
"Online safety cannot be solved by any one company. Bad actors move between platforms, and a child's online life spans many apps, games, and services."
The US Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism began its investigation into Roblox in August, requesting records related to child safety, sexual or physical abuse, bullying, and financial exploitation.
In a letter to Baszucki, Hawley and Durbin said the "alleged criminal activity on Roblox warrants congressional scrutiny."
"You trumpet Roblox as a safe digital playground for children as young as five," the senators wrote. "But the public record raises serious questions about this promise of safety."
"Over the past decade, police have arrested numerous individuals for committing serious acts of violence and harm against children they met via Roblox, including grooming, sexual abuse, kidnapping, rape, and even murder [...] children on your platform are hurting. Congress will not look the other way."
Roblox has implemented several new safety tools in recent years, such as restricting users under 13 from direct messaging, introducing global facial recognition checks, adding a "sensitive issues" content tag for experiences, and strengthening moderation policies and actions.

news.title: The future of British gaming is more than just games | Opinion
news.summary_raw: The UK has one of the most creative and innovative video games industries in the world. From independent studios developing original ideas to established businesses creating globally recognised franchises, British developers have consistently shown that they can compete on the international stage.

members.title: The future of British gaming is more than just games | Opinion

news.body:
The future of British gaming is more than just games | Opinion
As gaming brands became a fixture in TV, movies and pop culture, the industry and the government needs to support IP rather than individual releases, says Rebellion CEO and co-founder Jason Kingsley
The UK has one of the most creative and innovative video games industries in the world. From independent studios developing original ideas to established businesses creating globally recognised franchises, British developers have consistently shown that they can compete on the international stage.
The Government rightly recognises the creative industries as a priority growth sector, and over the past two decades we’ve seen a significant improvement in how policymakers engage with our industry. There is now a much greater understanding of the economic contribution games make, the highly skilled jobs they support and their potential as a major British export.
But as the industry evolves, we need to ensure the policies designed to support it evolve too.
We have an opportunity to have a much bigger conversation about how the UK supports the development and ownership of British intellectual property.
Entertainment is changing
Traditionally, video games, film, television and publishing have been treated as distinct industries, each with their own business models, funding structures and tax incentives. Now the boundaries between them are becoming blurred.
A successful video game can become a hit television series. A comic book character can inspire a major film franchise. A compelling fictional universe can find audiences across multiple formats, platforms and generations. At Rebellion, this is something we understand first-hand.
Alongside developing and publishing video games, we own 2000 AD, the home of iconic characters including Judge Dredd and Rogue Trooper. We also operate across comics, books, film and television, bringing stories and characters to life in different ways. Our recent Rogue Trooper film is an example of how intellectual property can move between creative formats, reaching new audiences while building on an established British franchise.
For businesses like ours, these aren't separate industries. They're different expressions of the same underlying intellectual property, supported by teams of talented people working across disciplines.
Yet the UK's system of creative tax reliefs remains largely organised around individual formats. We have incentives for video games, film, television and other forms of production, but comparatively little recognition of the intellectual property that connects them.
Backing British IP
Creating a successful game, character or fictional universe can take years of investment, experimentation and risk. But when an idea succeeds, its value can extend well beyond the format in which it was originally created. For British studios, the opportunity is to build the next globally recognised entertainment franchise and, critically, to retain ownership of that intellectual property here in the UK.
We only need to look across the Atlantic to see the potential. American entertainment giants like Disney and Marvel have built global businesses around characters and stories that span films, television, games and publishing. There is no reason why Britain cannot build more businesses with similar ambitions, developing homegrown intellectual property into franchises that reach audiences around the world.
When British businesses own their IP, they have greater control over how it is developed, licensed and commercialised. They can reinvest the returns into new projects, create skilled jobs and build sustainable businesses that continue to generate value over decades. This is particularly important for independent developers, who often face difficult decisions about how to fund ambitious projects while retaining control of the ideas they create.
There is no simple solution, and any reform would need to recognise the different economics of games, film, television and publishing. But I believe there is a strong case for the Government to explore how existing creative tax incentives could better support businesses developing intellectual property across multiple formats.
That means asking whether the framework we have today properly reflects how modern creative businesses operate, and whether it does enough to encourage long-term investment in British-owned IP.
The future of the industry
The UK already has many of the ingredients needed to build the next generation of global entertainment franchises, like exceptional creative talent, world-class studios, a strong independent development community and a rich history of storytelling.
The challenge now is ensuring that the businesses creating those franchises have the support and confidence to scale internationally while remaining rooted in Britain.
Government engagement with the games industry has come a long way, and that progress should be recognised. Now we have an opportunity to build on it. If we want Britain to remain a global leader in creative innovation, we need to think beyond individual games, films or television productions, and recognise the long-term value of the intellectual property that connects them.

news.body:
由于大多数单机游戏都调整了发售日，这个时间段最可能被影响到的是一些大型网游的日活。
前几天出门逛街，在本地电玩店，竟然看到了专门制作摆在门口的灯箱，提醒我去店里预购那个游戏的实体版。虽然我们这里实际上并不能走官方渠道预购，还得分辨是不是原封，可这个气氛算是烘托起来了。
那个游戏最近的数据强到可怕。过去一周，关于预购数量的统计已经从1200万份飙升到1500万份，预估收入约14.5亿美元。作为对比，前作正式发售首周的销量约为1100万份，也就是说，目前仅靠预购，它已经超越了前作的整个首周表现。
索尼和微软均确认，那个游戏是两大主机平台历史上预订量最高的游戏，其中索尼占比约为75%，遥遥领先。
一项调查显示，约8%的美国成年玩家计划为那个游戏调整工作或学习安排，其中大部分人准备请假一天或一天以上。也有一些开明的公司宣布暂时放假，让员工打个昏天黑地再回来工作。
总之，那个游戏明天就要上市了，甚至在一些比较快的时区，比如新西兰，今晚7点就会解锁。最近一阵子，我和我周围的人士很明显感到了被它影响的气氛。更别说现在距离玩到已经开始按小时计，所以不仅是电玩店，只要你有几个朋友，或者还活跃在某个游戏内、某个玩家社区中，总会感受到那个游戏要来了。
有的佛系网游，过去大家赛季初突击刷一刷过后就比较无聊，现在谈论起来，就是“正好去玩那个游戏”。有一些比较“肝”的，就会换个画风，比如近来风评几乎落入谷底的《EA Sports FC 27》，不仅因为游戏风骚的运营导致人气凋零，连热门评论区都是“再没起色，等那个游戏一来”的情绪。
这个情绪似曾相识。几周前，《FC 27》玩友们的口头禅还是“再没起色，等《影零》一来”。我的体感是，《影之刃零》确实带走了一些朋友，导致我在白天匹配对战偶尔会找不到对手，那么那个游戏的声量又远远大过叶师傅，想必能真正带走的人还是非常壮观的。
别小看主机大作玩家的重合程度，玩足球游戏的未必就不玩其他类型，只不过足球网游确实太容易沉浸，过于“肝”，导致大家没有那么多时间去玩别的。我有一位踢球认识的朋友，暂时戒了“FC”系列以后，一个月至少能白金一款游戏。相比之下，如果去足球游戏里赶进度，那么一年能玩的就只有这一款了。
所以，当大量玩家十几年如一日等待的大作要发售了，你说EA心里慌不慌呢？
其他厂商看到那个游戏会选择避让，就像过去绕着《赛博朋克2077》，或是《黑神话：悟空》走那样。当大家形成共识，有个游戏可能口碑很好，销量不错，选择避一避风头当然是明智的。
这里面有些厂商会选择提前发售，因为本身开发进度就有富余，或者稍微赶一赶就可以提前。《死亡搁浅2：冥滩之上》就是把原定发售日硬生生调整到2025年6月，躲开原本定在9月上市的那个游戏，可那个游戏竟然自己跳票到了2026年11月，这不仅让小岛秀夫白提前了几个月，还导致今年假日季发售的大作们得重新思考发行策略。
《漫威金刚狼》《控制：共振》已经提前到今年9月发，甚至体量不足的《寂静岭：陨落小镇》也是，《影之刃零》晚一些，卡在了10月29日，大概也不能再晚了。另一些游戏，比如重启的《寓言》，以及《堕落之主2》推迟到了明年年初。虽然不算太好的档期，总归比留在11月，被那个游戏彻底淹没了好得多。
当然也有一些游戏就是头铁，那个游戏哪天上，它也哪天上，这就基本上属于行为艺术的范畴了。反正它的类型几乎不构成竞品，体量不足以形成威胁，简单来说，就是有没有那个游戏，它该不火还是不火，那么何不把同一天发售当做卖点，先来赚一拨吆喝呢？
那么我猜，由于大多数单机游戏都调整了发售日，这个时间段最可能被影响到的是一些大型网游的日活。手游用户重合度大概不高，但大型网游用户里同时还玩主机的就多了去了。到底是不是这样，等那个游戏发售了，让数据来说话吧，很快就可以揭晓答案。
最后我来回答“EA心里慌不慌”的问题，我感觉是不慌——游戏性调整越调越烂，核心的抽卡部分暴率低得惊人，黑五前后的活动也令人提不起任何兴趣，关于这一代“FC”系列到底有多烂，可以单开一个夜话历数罪状。不由得感叹EA家底是真厚，它还能折腾多久呢……

20th November 2026 - Link Blog
Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube). Claire Vo runs ChatPRD, an AI platform that helps product managers "turn an idea into a spec". The product has been live since the GPT-4 era, and Claire has been building it in public for much of that time.
In this YouTube video (see also the accompanying Twitter post) Claire describes the flood of token fraud she has seen from groups abusing the product's free trial, sometimes just to get free AI usage but often to resell tokens or run other commercial enterprises on top of the ChatPRD agent.
I am funding a international Roblox and Fortnite map studio. They run a loop of free trials and promo codes and then tunnel to my agent and use it to build Roblox and Fortnite maps.
Apparently one of the common prompts Claire saw running through her agent involved SVGs of pelicans riding bicycles! Presumably the token scammers are using that to help sniff the underlying models - different model families have a definite signature, and I've used it like this in the past to try and guess the identity of stealth preview models on platforms like OpenRouter.
Claire is winding down her free trials entirely, which sadly looks like the right decision in the face of this abuse.

members.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released

ai.body:
19th November 2026 - Link Blog
PostgreSQL 19 Released (via) Most years PostgreSQL ships a new release in September, but this year's release came two months later thanks mainly to the flurry of issues that the PostgreSQL team needed to address as part of the ongoing AI-reported vulnerability apocalypse.
This release was definitely worth the wait. My favorite new feature is this one:
For applications that send reads to standbys, PostgreSQL 19 adds "read-your-writes" consistency with the new
WAIT FOR LSN
command. A session on a standby can useWAIT FOR LSN
to wait until the standby has replayed the write-ahead log (WAL) up to a specific log sequence number (LSN) before running a query, so the application can read data it just wrote on the primary.
In practice, that looks like this:
UPDATE movie SET genre = 'Dramatic' WHERE genre = 'Drama';
SELECT pg_current_wal_insert_lsn();
That returns a value like 0/0306EE20
. Store that somewhere (a signed cookie would work) such that on a subsequent request your application can do:
WAIT FOR LSN '0/0306EE20' WITH (TIMEOUT '0.1s');
SELECT * FROM movie WHERE genre = 'Drama';
The timeout is optional - if you provide one you'll get an error if the replica you are talking to doesn't catch up within the specified time.
I first encountered this pattern in Wikipedia, which has a hand-rolled version of this built against MySQL replication:
In addition to this, MediaWiki attempts to ensure that the user sees events occurring on the wiki in chronological order. A few seconds of lag can be tolerated, as long as the user sees a consistent picture from subsequent requests. This is done by saving the primary binlog position in the session, and then at the start of each request, waiting for the replica to catch up to that position before doing any reads from it.
Here's the relevant MediaWiki code, which these days uses MySQL's WAIT_FOR_EXECUTED_GTID_SET() function and falls back to SOURCE_POS_WAIT().
